method: Read the LaTeX statements and proofs, the records of docs/, and the Lean signatures and relevant proof bodies. Literature statements below are the local Prop hypotheses with their recorded citations. The no-exact-overlaps argument of Example 4.5 is the prefix-cancellation and equal-length concatenation argument of the Lean proof. No LaTeX compilation was run.
dependency_convention: direct_literature_hypotheses lists the named cited Prop binders on the primary library declaration of the entry. hms, hfk, hfi, hfib and hfjj are theorems of the library (morrisShmerkinLyapunov_holds, equilibriumGibbs, fengInfoSum_holds, fengInfoSumBar_holds, fraserJordanJurgaDecomposition_holds) that Solution supplies, and hlyb follows from hly (fengLedrappierYoungBar_of_fengLedrappierYoung), which Solution supplies in the same way; hfk is the binder of EquilibriumGibbsStatement. paper_level_literature_hypotheses lists the cited predicates needed from the manuscript's hypotheses; it omits hms, hfk, hfi, hfib, hfjj and hlyb, and lists hly where an entry uses hlyb. hfk with hfjj constructs an internal GibbsDecomposition, which is never itself a literature hypothesis. Lists do not include Lean's standard axioms or Mathlib results.

hms.citation: Morris–Shmerkin, Theorem 3.1 (arXiv:1602.08789v3; Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 371 (2019))
hms.statement: Every invariant probability s-equilibrium state of a box-like tuple with rotations and a proximal diagonal generator has λ₂<λ₁ for 0<s<2. A theorem of the library: morrisShmerkinLyapunov_holds (BoxLike/MorrisShmerkin.lean), along Morris–Shmerkin, Lemmas 3.4 and 3.5, with no literature premise. Library statements that take it as a hypothesis receive this proof in Solution; no headline takes it.

hfk.citation: The Gibbs bounds of thm:irred_eq_state, which the article quotes from Feng–Käenmäki, Proposition 1.2 (arXiv:1009.3129; Discrete Contin. Dyn. Syst. 30 (2011)), for irreducible tuples
hfk.statement: For a box-like tuple with rotations and 0<s<2, every invariant probability s-equilibrium state has the two-sided singular-value Gibbs bounds. A theorem of the library: equilibriumGibbs (BoxLike/EquilibriumGibbs.lean), with no literature premise; every such state equals the image of Bowen's ergodic Gibbs measure under forgetting the orientation. Library statements that take it as a hypothesis receive this proof in Solution; no headline takes it.
hfk.irreducible_form: FengKaenmakiGibbs (BoxLike/Literature.lean:86), the same conclusion for irreducible box-like tuples; a theorem of the library (fengKaenmakiGibbs_holds, BoxLike/QuasiMultiplicative/Main.lean), from FengKaenmakiNormEquilibrium (fengKaenmakiNormEquilibrium_holds); no result of this section takes it.

hfjj.citation: Fraser–Jordan–Jurga, Lemma 1.3 and Corollaries 1.5, 1.6 (arXiv:1706.06833; J. Fractal Geom. 7 (2020))
hfjj.statement: For a box-like tuple with rotations and a proximal diagonal generator, 0<s<2, and an invariant probability μ with the singular-value Gibbs bounds, there exist ergodic scalar Gibbs measures μ₁,μ₂ with the four restricted-coding decompositions and λ₁(μ)=barλ(μ₁), λ₂(μ)=barλ(μ₂). No separation condition. A theorem of the library: fraserJordanJurgaDecomposition_holds (BoxLike/FraserJordanJurga/Main.lean), with no literature premise; the hypothesis HasProximalDiagonal is not used. Library statements that take it as a hypothesis receive this proof in Solution; no headline takes it.
hfjj.gibbs_existence: The existence of the ergodic Gibbs measures on the mixing Sigma_Z is Bowen's theorem, which the library proves with no literature input (bowenGibbsExistence, existsUnique_ergodic_isGibbsPotential, BoxLike/Bowen/); the proof of the predicate starts from it (System.exists_isGibbs_potential₁).
hfjj.proof: Bowen's theorem (bowenGibbsExistence) gives the ergodic Gibbs measure μ₁ for f_{1,s} on the mixing Σ_Z (System.exists_isGibbs_potential₁), and μ₂ is its image under the exchange of the axes (System.isGibbs_potential₂_map_flipAxis); the image of μ₁ under forgetting the axis has the Gibbs bounds of φ^s, since each word has two lifts and φ^s(A_w) is the larger of the two exponentials (System.hasGibbsBounds_map_unCode); every invariant measure with the Gibbs bounds equals this ergodic measure (System.eq_of_hasGibbsBounds); the four decompositions follow from Σ_Z = τ(Σ) ⊔ ω(Σ) and the exchange of the two ranges; the Lyapunov identities follow from Birkhoff's theorem along the two lifts and the relative-entropy comparison \overline{λ}(𝖠, μ₂) ≤ \overline{λ}(𝖠, μ₁) (System.lyapunov_map_unCode_of_isGibbs).

hjr.citation: Jordan–Rapaport, Theorem 1.1 (arXiv:1908.00271; Proc. Lond. Math. Soc. 122 (2021))
hjr.statement: Under projective exponential separation, every ergodic invariant probability ν on the scalar full shift projects to an exact-dimensional measure of dimension min(1,−entropy ν/lyapBar ν). Both signs of nonzero contraction ratio are allowed.

hfi.citation: Feng, Lemma 4.6, first identity of (4.16) (arXiv:1901.01691v2; Duke Math. J. 172 (2023))
hfi.statement: For an invariant ergodic probability μ with λ₂<λ₁, the negative logarithm of each conditional n-cylinder mass for ξ_i is the n-term information sum, for every n on one conull set. A theorem of the library: fengInfoSum_holds (BoxLike/FengIdentity.lean), proved along Feng's Lemmas 4.4 and 4.5. Library statements that take it as a hypothesis receive this proof in Solution; no headline takes it.

hfib.citation: Feng, Lemma 4.6, first identity of (4.16) (arXiv:1901.01691v2; Duke Math. J. 172 (2023))
hfib.statement: For a proximal box-like system with rotations and any invariant probability ν supported on Σ_Z, including nonergodic ν, the scalar conditional n-cylinder information identity holds for every n on one conull set. A theorem of the library: fengInfoSumBar_holds (BoxLike/FengIdentityBar.lean), proved along Feng's Lemmas 4.4 and 4.5 without the constant-multiplicity hypothesis, rotations or proximality. Library statements that take it as a hypothesis receive this proof in Solution; no headline takes it.

hly.citation: Feng, Theorems 1.2 and 1.3 (arXiv:1901.01691v2; Duke Math. J. 172 (2023))
hly.statement: For an invariant ergodic probability μ on a box-like System with λ₂<λ₁, π_*μ is exact-dimensional of dimension (h₁−h₀)/λ₁+(h₂−h₁)/λ₂. The box-like specialisation of the manuscript's first clause, which the headlines take.
hly.implied_by: Implied by the authorised PlanarFengLedrappierYoung (PlanarFengLedrappierYoung.fengLedrappierYoung, BoxLike/LiteraturePlanarFeng.lean), the first part of thm:feng1 for every planar self-affine set; the headlines take this box-like form.

hly_planar.citation: Feng, Dimension of invariant measures for affine iterated function systems, Duke Math. J. 172 (2023), Theorems 1.2 (ii) and 1.3, formula (1.6) (arXiv:1901.01691v2)
hly_planar.statement: Universally over finite discrete alphabets and planar self-affine systems P (PlanarSystem: invertible contracting linear parts): for a shift-invariant ergodic probability mu with lambda2 < lambda1, mu.map P.proj is exact-dimensional of dimension (h1-h0)/lambda1 + (h2-h1)/lambda2, with hi = P.dimEntropy mu i.
hly_planar.source_boundary: Source: an affine IFS on R^d, not necessarily invertible or contracting; an ergodic m on the two-sided full shift for which the system is average contracting; the distinct Lyapunov exponents with multiplicities k_i; local dimensions with closed Euclidean balls; the entropies h_i = H_m(P | xi_i-hat) of (1.5). Specialisation: d = 2, invertible contractions, mu ergodic with lambda2 < lambda1, so that s = 2, k_1 = k_2 = 1 and (1.6) is (h1-h0)/lambda1 + (h2-h1)/lambda2. Feng's entropies for his partitions on a Borel set of full measure inside the library's Sigma' are the library's (PlanarSystem.condEntropy_fengXi_eq), so the source statement implies the transcription (planarFengLedrappierYoung_of_fengXi, proved). Closed supremum-norm balls give the same pointwise dimension as Euclidean balls; the order of the matrix products and the signs agree with Feng's (1.3), Section 1.2 and (1.6). Degenerate instances, by hand: one letter with A = diag(1/2, 1/4) (Dirac projection, all h_i = 0); zero translations with a Bernoulli measure (both sides 0); scaled rotations (lambda1 = lambda2, the statement is silent).
hly_planar.reductions: PlanarFengLedrappierYoung.fengLedrappierYoung (the box-like predicate FengLedrappierYoung, through System.toPlanar); planarFengLedrappierYoung_of_fengXi (the source form for Feng's partitions implies the statement).
hly_planar.downstream_uses: PlanarSystem.feng1 and planar_feng1 (Theorem 4.2, thm:feng1, at the article's scope) and the reduction to FengLedrappierYoung; no headline result, which takes FengLedrappierYoung.

hlyb.citation: Feng, Theorems 1.2 and 1.3 (arXiv:1901.01691v2; Duke Math. J. 172 (2023))
hlyb.statement: For a proximal box-like system with rotations and an invariant ergodic probability ν supported on Σ_Z, barπ_*ν is exact-dimensional of dimension (barh₁−barh₀)/barλ. It follows from FengLedrappierYoung: fengLedrappierYoungBar_of_fengLedrappierYoung (BoxLike/ProjectiveLineSystem.lean), through the planar system z ↦ diag(g'_j, g'_j/2) z + (g_j(0), 0) of the projective system, for every box-like system, with neither rotations nor proximality (System.isExactDim_map_projBar_of_fengLedrappierYoung). Library statements that take it as a hypothesis receive this proof in Solution; no headline takes it.

hfh.citation: Feng–Hu, Theorem 2.8 (arXiv:1002.2036v1; Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 62 (2009))
hfh.statement: Every scalar self-similar projection of an ergodic invariant probability measure is exact-dimensional without separation. Used by the unnumbered no-separation remark; unnecessary for the separated numbered theorems because Jordan–Rapaport already includes exact-dimensionality.

entries.label: thm:exact-dimensional-mixture
entries.other_hypotheses: Finite Borel measures on a metric space with the Besicovitch covering property; nonzero assumptions only where positive occurrence/uniqueness needs them. Finite-dimensional real normed spaces satisfy the required type classes.
entries.fidelity: All four conclusions, including positive occurrence of each distinct value, are represented. The real-space specialization of the generic lemmas matches the manuscript.
proof_deviations: The manuscript omits the proof. Lean supplies the Radon–Nikodym/Besicovitch differentiation proof, which proves the asserted componentwise local dimensions.

entries.label: thm:feng1
entries.other_hypotheses: Planar clause: every planar self-affine system (PlanarSystem), an invariant ergodic probability and λ₂<λ₁. Scalar clause: proximal box-like System with rotations, an invariant ergodic probability carried by Σ_Z; its proof needs neither rotations nor proximality. Proved input: BoxLike.FengLedrappierYoungBar (`fengLedrappierYoungBar_of_fengLedrappierYoung`, the second part of thm:feng1 from FengLedrappierYoung, proved in BoxLike/ProjectiveLineSystem.lean); `planar_feng1` takes it as a hypothesis and `paper_4_2_10` discharges it from BoxLike.PlanarFengLedrappierYoung.
entries.fidelity: both clauses at the article's scope (`planar_feng1`), as cited results; the article gives no proof. The planar clause for every planar self-affine set is the authorised `PlanarFengLedrappierYoung` (BoxLike/LiteraturePlanarFeng.lean, `PlanarSystem.feng1`); the headlines take the box-like specialisation `FengLedrappierYoung` (`PlanarFengLedrappierYoung.fengLedrappierYoung`). The scalar clause `FengLedrappierYoungBar` follows from `FengLedrappierYoung` through the planar system z ↦ diag(g'_j, g'_j/2) z + (g_j(0), 0) of the projective system (`fengLedrappierYoungBar_of_fengLedrappierYoung`; `System.isExactDim_map_projBar_of_fengLedrappierYoung` for every box-like system), so both clauses follow from `PlanarFengLedrappierYoung` alone (`paper_4_2_11`). Feng's partitions on his admissible set have almost everywhere the same conditional measures as the partitions of the library (`PlanarSystem.condMeas_fengXi_ae_eq`), so the source statement implies the transcription (`planarFengLedrappierYoung_of_fengXi`).
proof_deviations: Cited result, no manuscript proof. Lean uses closed sup-norm balls; equivalence with Euclidean local dimension is mathematical background in the transcription, not a separate source axiom.

Feng's partitions on his admissible set have almost everywhere the same conditional measures as the partitions of the library (`System.condMeas_fengXi_ae_eq`, `PlanarSystem.condMeas_fengXi_ae_eq`), so the entropies agree.

The second clause follows from the first, by an argument the manuscript does not give: the planar system z ↦ diag(g'_j, g'_j/2) z + (g_j(0), 0) over the alphabet ι × ZMod 2 has its attractor on the horizontal axis, the projection 𝐣 ↦ (\overline{π}(𝐣), 0), the exponents \overline{λ} and \overline{λ} - log 2, partitions ξ_2 = ξ_1 and entropies h_i = \overline{h}_i, so the planar formula reduces to the scalar one for every box-like system, with neither rotations nor proximality (`System.isExactDim_map_projBar_of_fengLedrappierYoung`).

entries.label: thm:entropy_eq_gibbs
entries.other_hypotheses: The entropy-rate helpers take hdec : S.GibbsDecomposition s μ μ₁ μ₂. The paper has rotations, a proximal diagonal generator, 0<s<2, and the equilibrium state. hdec supplies the two Gibbs measures, ergodicity and factor decompositions. To derive hdec from the equilibrium-state hypotheses use hfk and hfjj. Proved input: BoxLike.EquilibriumGibbsStatement (`equilibriumGibbs`, the Gibbs bounds of Proposition 3.10 for tuples with rotations, proved in BoxLike/EquilibriumGibbs.lean); the library statements take it as a hypothesis and Solution discharges it. Proved input: BoxLike.FraserJordanJurgaDecomposition (`fraserJordanJurgaDecomposition_holds`, Proposition 3.14, proved in BoxLike/FraserJordanJurga/); the library statements take it as a hypothesis and Solution discharges it.
entries.fidelity: The existing named helpers conclude equality of entropy rates, while the printed result uses conditional-past entropies. PastEntropy contains both bridges; the planar conull-set condition follows from ergodicity, which follows from hdec. No hms is necessary if the primed bridge is used. The literal endpoint dimEntropy_zero_eq_gibbs assembles both conditional-entropy identities.
proof_deviations: The proof follows the two-to-one coding argument of the prose: block entropies differ by at most log 2 and division by n removes this difference. The final equality with conditional-past entropy is separately proved by chain rule, Lévy upward convergence and Cesàro in PastEntropy.
